title: Determination of Infectious Lentiviral Titers with GFP-Encoding Lentivirus
author: Susanna C. Concilio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcbsisne
materials: Determination of infectious lentiviral titers with GFP-encoding lentivirus
Count at least 50,000 cells per replicate.
Six well plate: Corning Falcon, Corning, NY, #353046

steps.title: Dilute viral stock
steps.instruction: Dilute the pHR‑SFFV‑GFP‑IRES‑PGK‑PURO lentiviral stock 1:25 in OPTI‑MEM.

steps.title: Infect HeLa cells with serial virus volumes
steps.instruction: Add 0, 1, 5, 25, 125, and 375 µl of the diluted virus to duplicate wells of a six‑well plate that each contain 2 × 10⁵ HeLa cells in 1 ml DMEM supplemented with 10 % heat‑inactivated FBS, 1 % penicillin/streptomycin, and 1 % antibiotic/antimycotic.

steps.title: Incubate infected cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates for 72 hours post‑infection at standard cell‑culture conditions.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: After 72 hours, trypsinize the cells and wash them with 3 ml room‑temperature PBS.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Fix the washed cells by adding 500 µl 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS and incubate for 10 minutes at 37 °C.

steps.title: Wash cells with FACS buffer
steps.instruction: Wash the fixed cells twice with 3 ml cold FACS buffer (PBS + 1 % FBS + 0.1 % sodium azide, filtered through a 0.22 µm membrane).

steps.title: Store cells before analysis
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cells in FACS buffer and store them until flow‑cytometry analysis.

steps.title: Analyze GFP+ cells by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Run the stored cells on a flow cytometer and record the percentage of GFP‑positive cells.

steps.title: Calculate infectious titer
steps.instruction: Convert the GFP‑positive percentage to a decimal, then multiply by the number of cells (200 000), the initial virus‑volume factor (e.g., 25 µl), and the second dilution factor (e.g., 40) to obtain infectious particles per milliliter. Average the titers from the wells that give similar values (typically the 5, 25, and 125 µl dilutions).
